3. It is then stated that the impugned judgment and decree was passed on 18.3.01 and that the decree was signed on 25,3,01 but unfortunately the petitioner No. 1 became ill with Jaundice on 26.3.01and he was bedridden and was under the treatment of a local Kabiraj till I6A.02 and that the petitioner being aired on 17.4.02 applied for the certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree which was made ready on 27,4.02 and the petitioner then met the learned Advocate at Dhaka who then instructed the petitioner to obtain the certified copy of the judgment and decree of the trial court and accordingly the plaintiff applied for the same on 29.4.02 and obtained delivery of the judgment and decree of. the trial court on 18.5,02 but unfortunately the petitioner again become ill and he was bedridden as well as under treatment till 4.6.02 and having recovery to extent the petitioner met the learned Advocate on 5.6.02 and handed over all the necessary papers for filing revisional application which , in the meantime, became out of time by 350 days. The petitioner accordingly states that he had no lathes or inaction in filing the revisional application and that he may be allowed a chance so that he could file a revisional application against the judgment and decree dated 18,3.01 passed by the Additional District Judge, Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 753 of 1999. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the opposite party has filed affidavit in opposition and denied all the facts stated in the application for condonation of delay. The affidavit-in-opposition contains a certificate issued on 29,10.02 from the Chairman of Kunda Union Parishad to show that the opposite party No. 2, one Md. Bandur Mia died on 12.2.02. It is also alleged in the counter-affidavit that the petitioner was not sick and that he was not suffering from Jaundice and did not produce any certificate in support Of his illness. Mr. Rashid submits that the opposite party has obtained a kabala executed and registered through court on the basis of a decree passed in a suit for specific performance of a contract but could not get delivery of possession as yet due to the issuance of the present rule. 

 7. I have considered the statements made in the application for condonation of delay and the statement made in the affidavit in opposition and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the opposite party. The petitioner alleged that he was suffering from Jaundice and was under the treatment of a local Kabiraj. Jaundice is normally treated by Kabiraj of the locality and normally the patients do not go to specialized doctor and got their treatment by the Kabiraj of the locality. The petitioner of course alleged that he was once again attacked with illness after he handed over the certified copy of the judgment and decree of the appellate court to the learned Advocate but did not disclosed nature of his illness and such illness of the petitioner continued for about 24 days and Mr. Rashid is correct in his submission that no medical certificate has been filed by the petitioner for his illness for about 26 days. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the opposite party and also considered the statements made by the petitioner. The petitioner has not been properly advised as appears from the record in asmuchas an affidavit-in-opposition was filed 13.1.03 but -unfortunately the petitioner was not advised to file affidavit-in-reply. Unfortunately the petitioner is not represented by the learned Advocate also. In any view since the petitioner has explained the reasons for the delay of 350 days which appear to be bonafide and satisfactory 1 am inclined to afford the petitioner an opportunity to test his fate by filing a revisional application against the impugned judgment and decree. Having given my anxious consideration I condone the delay and direct the petitioner to get motion hearing of the Civil Revision within 2 (two) months from date.
